To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the dynamic amplification factor of the steel plane frame is related to damping ratio, failure time of the column, and DCR.
dynamic amplification factor is related to damping ratio, failure time of member and DCR.

The maximum dynamic amplification factor is 2 when the structure is still elastic, but the amplifying factor is related to demand-capability ratio and it increases with increasing demand-capability ratio until dynamic divergence occurs when the structure yields and behave plastically.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the dynamic effect resulted from structural damage and it is of great significance to the design of structures with high seismic performance.
the dynamic effect of the structure with initial failure during progressive collapse, the results of which can be used for safety evaluation of the structure.
the effect of dynamic effect on the collapse process of a single-story plane frame with a failed column.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, dynamic amplifying factor is related to damping ratio, demand-capacity ratio and the failure of the member.
, the dynamic amplifying factor is related to the failure time, the damping ratio, the initial DCR and the ultimate DCR.
the dynamic effect during progressive collapse of a single-story plane frame is related to the failure time of a member, damping ratio of the structure, DCR and the failure location.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the dynamic effect during progressive collapse is not as significant as expected, and the dynamic response of the structure is more sensitive to the failure time of member than to the failure mode of member.
the dynamic effect is very important for the analysis of progressive collapse of steel structure, and the failure of the structure should be analyzed dynamically.
the dynamic amplification factor is related to the initial failure time of the column and the DCR of the structure.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the dynamic effect should be taken into consideration in the progressive collapse analysis of steel structures.
, for a structure that has a high DCR, the dynamic amplifying factor will be larger and dynamic divergence will occur more likely, which means the collapse will be accelerated and more severe.
dynamic effect should be considered in the design of progressive collapse resistant structures.
